question: For delivered order items, how many more days on average does delivery take when the seller is in a different state from the customer than when they are in the same state? Use fractional days from purchase to customer delivery.
sql:
WITH delivered AS (
    SELECT
        o.order_id,
        c.customer_state,
        s.seller_state,
        CASE WHEN c.customer_state = s.seller_state THEN 'same' ELSE 'different' END AS state_match,
        EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (o.order_delivered_customer_date - o.order_purchase_timestamp)) / 86400.0 AS delivery_days
    FROM orders o
    JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
    JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
    JOIN sellers s ON oi.seller_id = s.seller_id
    WHERE o.order_status = 'delivered'
      AND o.order_purchase_timestamp IS NOT NULL
      AND o.order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT
    AVG(CASE WHEN state_match = 'different' THEN delivery_days END) -
    AVG(CASE WHEN state_match = 'same' THEN delivery_days END) AS avg_day_difference
FROM delivered
plan:
- Filter orders to those with order_status = 'delivered' and join to customers on customer_id and to sellers via order_items.seller_id.
- Compute delivery time as the difference in days between order_purchase_timestamp and order_delivered_customer_date.
- Determine a flag indicating whether seller_state = customer_state (same) or not (different).
- Group by the same/different flag and calculate the average delivery time for each group.
- Subtract the average for same-state deliveries from the average for different-state deliveries to get the difference in average days.
